item.title: Palestinian child killed by Israeli gunfire in northern Gaza
item.description:
Palestinian child killed by Israeli gunfire in northern Gaza

A seven-year-old Palestinian child succumbed to his wounds on Sunday after being shot by Israeli forces in Jabalia refugee camp, north of the Gaza Strip, Wafa news reported.

Medical sources told Wafa and Al Jazeera that Jihad al-Ghandour died from injuries sustained on Saturday when Israeli forces shot him near al-Houja Street in Jabalia camp.

Medical sources announced earlier that the death toll from the Israeli genocide in Gaza since 7 October 2023 had risen to 74,377, with 175,398 Palestinians injured.

item.title: Former US official says Israeli demands made Gaza deal 'impossible for another six months'
item.description:
Former US official says Israeli demands made Gaza deal 'impossible for another six months'

A former senior US official has accused Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of delaying a captive exchange and ceasefire deal in Gaza in 2024 by "so many of his own conditions", which prevented an agreement for "another six months".

Phil Gordon, who served as national security adviser to former US Vice President Kamala Harris from March 2022 to January 2025, made the allegations in a post on X on Saturday.

“Netanyahu instead added so many of his own conditions - against the advice of his own security chiefs - that the deal became impossible for another six months,” Gordon wrote. 

He said nearly 9,000 more Palestinians were killed in that period and more Israeli captives died. 

Gordon said the added Israeli demands included keeping forces along Gaza’s entire border with Egypt and a new mechanism to screen Palestinians returning north.

Both were dropped in the deal finally concluded in January 2025.

Read more: Former US official says Israeli demands made Gaza deal 'impossible for another six months'

item.title: Senior military commander says Iran will continue to strike vessels ‘if necessary’
item.description:
Senior military commander says Iran will continue to strike vessels ‘if necessary’

Iranian forces will continue to strike vessels in the Strait of Hormuz “if necessary”, senior Iranian military commander and deputy army coordinator Habibollah Sayyari said on Sunday. 

“We have dealt blows to enemy vessels, and if something happens against Iran again, we will strike at them. We are not tied, and we have facilities and capabilities that are specific and general in the world,” he said in comments carried by Iranian media.

item.title: Rights group files ICC complaint against Israeli medical officials over torture of Palestinian detainees
item.description: The Hind Rajab Foundation filed a complaint with the International Criminal Court (ICC) against Israeli medical officials over torture and mistreatment of Palestinian detainees, Israeli media reported Saturday, Anadolu reports. The complaint targets the Israeli Medical Association, Health Ministry officials and medical personnel over abuses at the Sde Teiman military detention facility in southern Israel. According to the Israeli newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth, the Brussels-based rights group submitted the complaint to the ICC prosecutor under Article 15 of the Rome Statute. The foundation said that Israeli medical personnel and officials were involved in practices amounting to war crimes and crimes against humanity. – Allegations of systematic mistreatment Since October 2023, the Sde Teiman military base in Israel’s southern Negev desert has […]

item.title: 60 countries participate in historic Global Day of Action for Palestine
item.description: The Global Day of Action for Palestine called for today, 10th October, has received massive support worldwide. Convened by the Global Alliance for Palestine with the support of the Anti-Apartheid Movement (AAM) and SANED, this historic international mobilisation unites over 200 organisations through 325 mapped events across 60 countries and six continents. From London to capitals and cities worldwide, people of conscience are rising together to declare that the genocide and suffering of the Palestinian people will never be swept aside, and Israel’s illegal occupation will never be normalised. item.title: Palestinian president postpones legislative elections to Sept. 11, 2027
item.description: Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree Saturday setting presidential and legislative elections for Sept. 11, 2027, revoking an earlier decree that had scheduled legislative elections for Nov. 28, 2026, Anadolu reports. The decree calls on Palestinians, including those in the occupied West Bank and the Gaza Strip, to take part in simultaneous elections for the president of the State of Palestine and members of the Palestinian Legislative Council, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. item.title: Pillay’s defiance, Sharif’s disgrace: The prize, the praise, and the politics of prostration
item.description: The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has exposed two political universes: a South Africa that defies imperial power and Israeli impunity, and a nuclear-armed Pakistan whose prime minister has elevated subservience into an instrument of statecraft. History occasionally delivers a political verdict so devastating that satire becomes redundant. The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has produced precisely such a spectacle. On one side stands Navi Pillay, the formidable South African jurist who confronted apartheid and exposed Israel’s conduct in Gaza as genocide. On the other stands Shehbaz Sharif, prime minister of nuclear-armed Pakistan, who has repeatedly championed Donald Trump for the same distinction, apparently convinced that a president presiding over devastating wars deserves humanity’s highest honour for peace-making.
